findings.finding: probe_source joins the Terraform tool session governed by the closed terraform_grounding_receipt.schema.json, whose reason_detail is a CLOSED enum paired one-to-one with the generic reason, yet the plan introduces new abstention causes (cross-host redirect, oversized metadata, embedded URL credentials, literal IP, non-HTTPS, uncredentialed private target, download-URL rejection, non-registry/dynamic source) without defining a reason_detail value for any of them.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the registry probe's HTTP layer as a NEW body-reading seam (stdlib urllib, no new dependency) that reads+size-limits the response body to 1 MiB and returns it for schema validation, rather than describing it as reuse of the status-only deps.py:_http_get seam.
evidence: src/rebar/grounding/deps.py:303 `def _http_get(url, *, timeout=...) -> int:` returns only `int(resp.status)`; docstring: 'GET url and return its HTTP status code — the SOLE network seam.'

Plan requires body-dependent facts: 'a bounded HTTPS response is successful, size-limited, and schema-valid', 'malformed/oversized metadata -> parse_error', 'yields only count/digest/source-kind facts'
No body-returning HTTP seam exists in rebar.grounding (search for urlopen shows only deps.py:313 in grounding, returning status)
findings.finding: The plan claims registry probing reuses 'the existing fail-open HTTP seam/harness', but the only grounding HTTP seam (deps.py:_http_get) returns just an integer status code and cannot read, size-limit, or schema-validate a response body, nor inspect/reject redirects — all of which the registry-metadata requirements demand. The needed HTTP body-reading + redirect-controlling capability is new and should be scoped explicitly rather than described as a reuse.
findings.location: Scope > Registry metadata; 'Bound metadata to 1 MiB per response ... Use the existing fail-open HTTP seam/harness; no new HTTP dependency.'
scenarios: Implementer wires probe_source to _http_get and finds it returns no body, forcing an unplanned new seam mid-build
Oversized/malformed responses cannot be classified to parse_error because the body is never read/bounded by the existing seam
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the claim to 'a new body-reading grounding HTTP seam built on stdlib urllib (no new dependency), mirroring deps.py's single-seam/monkeypatch discipline' and specify that the seam returns (status, capped-body) with a 1 MiB read cap.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the redirect-control mechanism (a custom urllib redirect handler / opener that intercepts 3xx and refuses cross-host follows) so the token is never re-sent to a redirect target, since default urlopen auto-follows redirects.
evidence: Stdlib urllib.request.urlopen installs a default HTTPRedirectHandler that transparently follows 3xx; a plain GET cannot 'reject before sending a token' without a custom handler or opener
Plan text: 'Reject embedded URL credentials, literal IP targets, non-HTTPS services, and cross-host redirects' and AC5 'rejecting ... cross-host redirects before sending a token'
findings.finding: The requirement to 'reject cross-host redirects before sending a token' is not achievable with stdlib urllib.request.urlopen's default behavior, which auto-follows 3xx redirects (via the default HTTPRedirectHandler) and would re-attach the Authorization header to the redirect target. The plan does not name the custom redirect-handling mechanism needed to intercept the redirect before the token is sent.
findings.location: Scope > Registry metadata / Network-target AC; 'Reject ... cross-host redirects' and 'rejecting ... cross-host redirects before sending a token'
scenarios: A registry host 302s to a different host; default urllib follows it and resends the Authorization header, leaking the ambient token cross-host — the exact failure AC5 forbids
findings.suggested_fix: State that the seam installs a redirect handler that raises/aborts on any Location whose host differs from the requested host (and never re-attaches the Authorization header), classifying the redirect as network_error.
